about: The interior of the gallbladder: the glass wall in three pieces (fundus, body and neck), the stored bile drawn at a size that follows how full the bag is, the cystic duct with its spiral fold, and the first parts of the common hepatic duct and the common bile duct. Bile streams into the bag between meals and out to the duodenum after a fatty meal. The ducts are short stubs and the junction is drawn close to the neck so that everything stays inside the organ's outline; the sizes are chosen to read clearly rather than measured. The layers of the wall, the sphincter at the duodenal end and the liver's finer ducts are left out.

GH14.label: Hall JE, Hall ME. Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed. Elsevier, 2021.

GRAYS42.label: Standring S (ed). Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 42nd ed. Elsevier, 2020.

parts.label: Fundus
parts.summary: The rounded blind end of the gallbladder
parts.function: The fundus is the rounded end of the gallbladder, the part that projects furthest from the liver. It is drawn as glass so the stored bile shows through. It contracts and brightens when fat reaches the duodenum, and the whole bag shrinks around its neck.

drives.note: Fat in the duodenum releases a hormone that makes the gallbladder contract.
Contraction accompanies digestion of a meal.
Vagal drive adds to the contraction.

parts.label: Body
parts.summary: The main part of the bag, where bile is stored
parts.function: The body is the main storage part of the gallbladder. Between meals it fills with bile from the liver and concentrates it by absorbing water. After a fatty meal its smooth muscle contracts and squeezes bile out. It is drawn as glass, brightens with fat in the gut, and shrinks as it empties.

drives.note: Fat in the duodenum releases a hormone that makes the gallbladder contract.
Contraction accompanies digestion of a meal.
Vagal drive adds to the contraction.

parts.label: Neck
parts.summary: The narrowed end that bends into the cystic duct
parts.function: The neck is the tapering end of the gallbladder, which curves and narrows into the cystic duct. Bile enters and leaves the bag through it. It is drawn as glass and contracts with the rest of the wall.

drives.note: Fat in the duodenum releases a hormone that makes the gallbladder contract.
Contraction accompanies digestion of a meal.
Vagal drive adds to the contraction.

parts.label: Stored Bile
parts.summary: The bile held in the gallbladder, drawn to show how full it is
parts.function: Bile made by the liver is stored in the gallbladder between meals and becomes more concentrated as water is absorbed. Its size here follows how full the bag is: it is full between meals and shrinks when the gallbladder squeezes after a fatty meal.

drives.note: Fat in the gut empties the gallbladder.

parts.label: Cystic Duct
parts.summary: The short duct joining the gallbladder to the main bile duct
parts.function: The cystic duct connects the neck of the gallbladder to the common hepatic duct. Bile flows along it in both directions: into the gallbladder between meals, and out of it after a fatty meal. It is drawn as glass so its stream can be seen.

drives.note: Bile flows out through it after a fatty meal.

parts.label: Spiral Fold
parts.summary: The helical fold inside the cystic duct
parts.function: The lining of the cystic duct is raised into a spiral fold, sometimes called the spiral valve. It helps keep the duct open as the gallbladder fills and empties.

parts.label: Common Hepatic Duct
parts.summary: Carries bile down from the liver
parts.function: The right and left hepatic ducts leave the liver and join to form the common hepatic duct, which carries bile down towards the cystic duct. Its stream runs all the time, since the liver makes bile continuously, and brightens after a fatty meal.

drives.note: Bile output is needed to digest fat.

parts.label: Common Bile Duct
parts.summary: Carries bile on to the duodenum
parts.function: The common bile duct is formed where the cystic duct joins the common hepatic duct. It runs down behind the first part of the duodenum to deliver bile into the gut. After a fatty meal bile streams along it, from the liver and from the gallbladder together.

drives.note: Bile flows to the duodenum when fat is present.

parts.label: Hartmann's Pouch
parts.summary: A bulge on the underside of the gallbladder neck
parts.function: Hartmann's pouch is a small outpouching where the neck begins. It points towards the duodenum, and it is where a gallstone is most likely to lodge.

parts.label: Mucosal Folds
parts.summary: The ridges of the lining inside the gallbladder
parts.function: The lining of the gallbladder is thrown into many folds that form a honeycomb pattern. They give the lining a large surface for taking water out of the bile, which concentrates it.

parts.label: Cystic Artery
parts.summary: The artery that supplies the gallbladder
parts.function: The cystic artery usually comes from the right hepatic artery. Near the neck it divides into branches that run over the wall.

parts.label: Hepatopancreatic Ampulla (of Vater)
parts.summary: Where the bile duct and pancreatic duct meet
parts.function: The common bile duct and the main pancreatic duct join in a short dilated chamber, the ampulla, which opens into the duodenum. In life it lies in the duodenal wall, which is not drawn here.

parts.label: Sphincter of Oddi
parts.summary: The ring of muscle that guards the ampulla
parts.function: The sphincter of Oddi is a ring of smooth muscle round the end of the ampulla. Between meals it stays closed so bile backs up into the gallbladder, and after a fatty meal it relaxes to let bile and pancreatic juice into the gut.

parts.label: Serosa
parts.summary: The outer covering of the gallbladder wall
parts.function: The serosa is the thin layer of peritoneum on the free surface of the gallbladder. The side against the liver has no serosa and is attached to it instead.

parts.label: Perimuscular Connective Tissue
parts.summary: The loose tissue between muscle and serosa
parts.function: This connective-tissue layer lies outside the muscle and carries the blood vessels, lymph vessels and nerves of the wall.

parts.label: Muscularis (Smooth Muscle)
parts.summary: The thin muscle layer of the wall
parts.function: The muscle fibres of the wall run in several directions. They contract when fat in the duodenum releases a hormone, squeezing bile out through the cystic duct.

parts.label: Lamina Propria
parts.summary: The layer of connective tissue under the lining
parts.function: The lamina propria supports the epithelium and holds small vessels and nerves. It follows the folds of the lining.

parts.label: Columnar Epithelium
parts.summary: The single layer of tall cells that lines the lumen
parts.function: These cells take water and salts out of the bile and so concentrate it. They also secrete mucus that protects the lining from bile.
